The Superintending Consul at the
British Consulate-General told "The
Shanghai Times" yesterday even-
ing that a protest had just been
sent by the Consul-General to
Mayor Fu Siao-en, the head of the
City Government of Greater Shang-
hai, concerning the shooting on
Tifeng Road at 10 p.m. on Wednes-
day night.
The protest was lodged last night
over the action of a City Govern-
ment policeman who fired a shot
at a British subject in his car,
without apparent reason or warn-
ing. The Shanghai Municipal
Police report containing the full
particulars and details of the in-
cident was sent to the Consulate
yesterday afternoon After study-
ing this report the protest was
sent to the City Government.

British subject was driving his car

Road. At the Great Western Road
intersection, the Briton noticed the
City Government policeman on the
pavement, but the latter did not
make any sign to stop and the
Briton drove on down Tifeng
Road. Before he had reached the
end of the road in his car, how-
ever, he heard a loud rifle report
and a bullet whistled past his
motor car. The Briton was un-
injured and stepped on his
accelerator and continued down
Route Alfred Magy.
Later he reported the matter to
the British military authorities and
they notified the headquarters of
the Special Municipality Police
and demanded an explanation. No
reply was received yesterday and
so the protest was lodged by the
British Consul-General. The Brit-
ish military actually know the
number of the policeman concern-
ed. The British subject who was
the object of the shooting has kept
his name undisclosed.

英国驻上海总领事馆的监理领事昨晚告诉《字林西报》，总领事刚刚就周三晚10时在提封路发生的枪击事件，向大上海特别市政府市长傅筱庵提出抗议。

此次抗议是于昨晚提出的，针对的是一名市政府警察在无明显理由或警告的情况下，向一名坐在车内的英国臣民开枪的行为。包含该事件完整情况和细节的上海公共租界工部局警务处报告已于昨日下午送至领事馆。在研究该报告后，抗议照会被发送至市政府。

事件发生时，一名英国臣民正驾驶汽车沿提封路由北向南行驶。在大西路路口，这名英国人注意到人行道上有一名市政府警察，但后者未发出任何停车示意，该英国人便继续沿提封路行驶。然而，在他驾车尚未到达道路尽头之前，他听到一声巨大的步枪响声，一颗子弹呼啸着擦过他的汽车。该英国人未受伤，他踩下油门，继续沿阿尔弗雷德·马奇路（Route Alfred Magy）行驶。

随后，他向英国军方当局报告了此事，军方通知了特别市警察总部并要求解释。昨日未收到回复，因此英国总领事提出了抗议。英国军方实际上知道涉事警察的编号。遭到枪击的英国臣民选择不公开其姓名。

DEC 5 1938

British Patrol
Nabs 4 Puppet
Policemen

Four policemen of the "Shang-
hai City Government" who at-
tempted to intimidate a shroff of
the Danish-owned Shanghai Milk
Supply Co., Ltd., at 145 Tunsin
Road yesterday morning, were ar-
rested by a British military patrol.
At a late hour last night the pup-
pet police quartet was still repos-
ing in the Bubbling Well Police
Station.

Members of the Tsachoching
Station, the puppet police were at-
tempting to arrest the shroff to
take him back to headquarters,
where complaints had been filed
against him. However, they over-
stepped their rights when they at-
tempted to effect the arrest on an
extra-Settlement Road, which is
outside their jurisdiction.

The military patrol of Seaforth
Highlanders who were marching by
on their routine beat along Tunsin
Road at 10 a.m. yesterday, saw
the four men with pistols drawn
and immediately arrested them.
They were turned over to the
Shanghai Municipal Police and dis-
armed.

The shroff was one Mau Miao-
sah, owner of a factory in a Chi-
nese village off Tunsin Road,
whose business burned down re-
cently. Two neighboring houses
were destroyed in the course of
the fire, and the owners of these
homes are seeking damages from
Mau, it was learned last night.

Reason For Arrest

Unable to obtain satisfaction
from the shroff, the villagers ap-
pealed to the puppet police of
Tsachoching Station, resulting in
the attempted arrest of the
shroff by the "Ta Tao" officers on
Tunsin Road yesterday morning.

The puppet quartet was still
at Bubbling Well Station yester-
day, and it could not be learned
last night what action was being
contemplated by the authorities of
the Police and British Military.

It will be recalled that two Chi-
nese constables of the S.M.C. who
were arrested by Japanese gendar-
mes November 19 are still in
custody.

《大美晚报》
1938年12月5日

英国巡逻队
逮捕4名伪警察

昨天上午，四名“上海市政府”警察试图在通辛路145号恐吓丹麦所有的上海牛奶有限公司的一名出纳员，随后被英国军事巡逻队逮捕。直到昨晚深夜，这四名伪警察仍关押在静安寺捕房。

这些来自曹家渡分站的伪警察成员试图逮捕该出纳员，将其带回总部，因为有人对他提出了投诉。然而，当他们试图在一条越界筑路（超出其管辖范围）上实施逮捕时，他们越权了。

昨天上午10时，正在通辛路沿线进行例行巡逻的海福尔高地兵团（Seaforth Highlanders）军事巡逻队，看到这四人拔出手枪，立即逮捕了他们。他们被移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处并被解除武装。

该出纳员名为茅妙沙（Mau Miao-sah，音译），是通辛路外一个中国村庄的一家工厂主，其生意最近被烧毁。据悉，火灾过程中两栋邻近房屋被毁，这些房屋的业主正向茅某寻求赔偿。

逮捕原因

由于无法从该出纳员处获得满意的结果，村民们向曹家渡分站的伪警察求助，导致昨天上午“大陶”警官在通辛路试图逮捕该出纳员。

这四名伪警察昨天仍在静安寺捕房，昨晚尚不清楚警方和英国军方当局正在考虑采取何种行动。

回顾一下，11月19日被日本宪兵逮捕的两名工部局华籍巡捕目前仍被拘留。

CHINA PRESS.
DEC - 1939.
U.S. Consulate Lodges Protest
Over Attack On Ex-Army Officer
Japanese Wife
Is Slapped By
Puppet Police

While Japanese diplomats
were contemplating action "to
improve relations between
Washington and Tokyo, the
American Consulate-General
here yesterday morning filed yet
another protest with the Japan-
ese Consul-General.
The complaint was made
following the attack by puppet
"City Government" policemen
on Major John B. Penniston,
American Army officer in the
World War.
The representations which were
drawn up yesterday morning deal
exclusively with the assault on
Major Penniston, and no mention
was made of Mrs. Penniston, who
is Japanese as she is not an
American citizen.
Path Blocked
The incident occurred Sunday
afternoon while Major and Mrs.
Penniston was walking along Yu
Yuen Road, near Brenan Road,
with their infant son, who was in
a perambulator in charge of an
amah.
As they reached a point near
Brenan Road, they found their
path blocked by a group of six
puppet policemen. Mr. Pennis-
ton motioned them to stand
aside, and one officer, standing
in the middle of the sidewalk,
moved away. When Mrs. Pen-
niston and her amah pushing
the perambulator reached the
spot, however, the policeman
stuck his feet out and refused
to allow the baby-carriage to
pass.
Mr. Penniston attempted to pro-
test, but two of the policemen
threatened him with the rifles in
their hands. Meanwhile, his wife
was stopped by another policeman.
She also protested in Chinese, but
was not heeded.
Woman Slapped
According to Mrs. Penniston, the
officer told her that if she was
Japanese, she might pass. When
she did not reply as to her nation-
ality, she stated, she was slapped
on the face.
Major Penniston rushed over
to save his wife from further
manhandling, and was also as-
saulted, receiving blows from a
rifle butt which bruised his left
forearm. At the same time, an-
other policeman dealt Mrs.
Penniston several blows on her
shoulder, ripping her fur coat
with the muzzle of his rifle.
At this point one of the puppet
policemen attempted to intervene.
While he was talking with the other
policemen, Major Penniston helped
his wife with the baby and amah
to move on with Mrs. Penniston
still protesting in Chinese.
Apparently irritated by her words,
two puppet officers who had as-
saulted them moved toward her
threateningly, but were prevented
from approaching by a Chinese in
civilian clothes, whose identity was
still a mystery yesterday.

1939年12月。

美国领事馆就前陆军军官遇袭事件提出抗议
日籍妻子遭伪警掌掴

正当日本外交官 contemplating 采取“改善华盛顿与东京之间关系”的行动之际，美国驻沪总领事馆于昨日上午再次向日本总领事提出抗议。

此次投诉系因伪“市政府”警察袭击第一次世界大战期间的美军军官约翰·B·彭尼斯顿（John B. Penniston）少校而起。

昨日上午起草的交涉照会仅涉及对彭尼斯顿少校的袭击一事，未提及彭尼斯顿夫人，因其为日本人，并非美国公民。

道路受阻

事发于周日下午，当时彭尼斯顿夫妇正带着幼子沿愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）靠近贝当路（Brenan Road）处散步，幼子坐在婴儿车里，由一名阿妈（amah）照看。

当他们走到贝当路附近时，发现去路被六名伪警察挡住。彭尼斯顿先生示意他们让开，站在人行道中间的一名警官随即移开。然而，当彭尼斯顿夫人推着婴儿车偕同阿妈到达该处时，那名警察却伸出双脚，拒绝让婴儿车通过。

彭尼斯顿先生试图抗议，但其中两名警察用手中的步枪威胁他。与此同时，他的妻子被另一名警察拦住。她也用中文提出抗议，但未获理睬。

女子遭掌掴

据彭尼斯顿夫人称，那名警官告诉她，如果她是日本人，就可以通过。她表示，由于她未回答自己的国籍问题，结果挨了一记耳光。

彭尼斯顿少校冲上前去，以免妻子遭受进一步的粗暴对待，但他自己也遭到袭击，左前臂被枪托击打致淤青。与此同时，另一名警察用步枪枪口撕破了彭尼斯顿夫人的皮草大衣，并朝她的肩膀猛击数下。

此时，一名伪警察试图介入调解。在他与其他警察交谈之际，彭尼斯顿少校协助妻子、孩子和阿妈继续前行，彭尼斯顿夫人仍用中文抗议着。

显然被她的言语激怒，此前袭击他们的两名伪警察气势汹汹地向她逼近，但被一名身份不明的便衣中国人阻止，未能靠近。

CHINA PRESS.
DEC 4 - 1939
399 P
# 1/2 B

American Ex-Army Officer,
Japanese Wife, Assaulted
By "Ta Tao" Policemen

Victims On
Way To Park
With Infant

Puppet Officers Acted
Like "Savages," Says
Major Penniston

Major John B. Penniston, American Army officer during the World War, and his Japanese wife, were severely manhandled by six "Ta Tao" policemen on Yu Yuen Road near Brenan Road yesterday afternoon while accompanying their infant boy to Jessfield Park.

Both Major and Mrs. Penniston were assaulted by the puppet police, the former sustaining slight bruises on the arm while his wife received injuries about her shoulder. The fur coat which Mrs. Penniston was wearing was ripped by the rifle muzzle of one of the policemen.

In an interview with THE CHINA PRESS yesterday evening, Major Penniston described the "savage attitude" of the puppet officers and stated he "could not understand why arms were put in the hands of such men."

Act Like Savages

"Two of them acted like savages," the major recalled. "They were absolutely unreasonable in their attitude with the exception of one who was relatively decent."

Although neither of the victims required any hospital treatment, they were still in a painful condition last night. The bruised marks were clearly visible.

With his baby riding in a carriage under the care of a Chinese amah, the Major stated, he and his wife proceeded toward the park at about 2:30 p.m. When they reached the Yu Yuen Road and Brenan Road intersection they found the puppet officers blocking the sidewalk near to the park.

"As I motioned them to stand aside in order to make room for my family to pass," Mr. Penniston said, "the policeman, in the middle of the sidewalk moved away slightly. But when Mrs. Penniston and the carriage, immediately behind, reached the spot, the officer stuck his left foot in front of the carriage wheels preventing them from moving."

Later he registered a protest with the "Ta Tao" men, he recalled. And as he did so, two of the policemen threatened him with the rifles in their hands.

Wife Slapped

Meanwhile, his wife was stopped by another policeman. She also protested, the Major recalled, by uttering a few words in Chinese which he knowing no Chinese, did not understand.

While her protest went unheeded one of the policemen asked Mrs. Penniston, she later revealed, of her nationality. "If you are Japanese, go on, it's all right," the officer was stated to have said.

When she failed to reply to the inquiry, Major Penniston stated, the policeman slapped her squarely on the face without realizing that she was a Japanese woman.

In an attempt to protect his wife from further manhandling, Major Penniston rushed to her aid and protested vigorously to the officers again. His protest, however was answered by blow from a rifle butt, which bruised his left forearm. At the time, other policemen also rushed to his wife and dealt several blows to her shoulder, ripping her fur coat.

Puppet Interfered

It was at this point that one of the "Ta Tao" policemen attempted to stop the dispute. While he was so doing, the major stated, he helped his wife with the baby and the amah to move on with Mrs. Penniston still protesting.

Apparently irritated by the Chinese words which Mrs. Penniston spoke as she continued toward the park, the two officers who were responsible for slapping her on the face came storming at her again. The timely interference of a Chinese in civilian clothes, whose identity could not be ascertained, was believed to have prevented the staging of other assaults against the couple.

Following the incident, Major Penniston reported the case to the Bubbling Well Police Station. He said he would report the matter to the American Consular authorities today.

The major at one time served on the staff of THE CHINA PRESS.

美籍前陆军军官及其日籍妻子
遭“大道”警察殴打

受害者携幼子
前往公园途中

彭尼斯顿少校称
伪警行径如“野蛮人”

第一次世界大战期间的美军军官约翰·B·彭尼斯顿（John B. Penniston）少校及其日籍妻子，于昨日下午在陪同幼子前往兆丰公园（Jessfield Park）途中，在愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）近贝当路（Brenan Road）处，遭到六名“大道”（Ta Tao）警察的严重粗暴对待。

彭尼斯顿夫妇均遭伪警察殴打，前者手臂轻微淤青，后者肩部受伤。彭尼斯顿夫人身穿的皮草大衣被其中一名警察的步枪枪口撕裂。

彭尼斯顿少校昨晚在接受《字林西报》采访时，描述了伪警察的“野蛮态度”，并表示他“无法理解为何将武器交给这样的人”。

行如野蛮人

“其中两人的行为如同野蛮人，”少校回忆道。“除了一个相对得体的人外，他们的态度完全不可理喻。”

虽然两名受害者均无需住院治疗，但昨晚他们仍处于痛苦之中。淤痕清晰可见。

少校称，当时他的孩子坐在婴儿车里，由一名中国阿妈照看，他和妻子于下午2时30分左右前往公园。当他们到达愚园路与贝当路交汇处时，发现伪警察 blocking 了公园附近的人行道。

“当我示意他们让开，以便让我的家人通过时，”彭尼斯顿先生说，“站在人行道中间的警察稍微移开了一点。但是，当彭尼斯顿夫人和紧随其后的婴儿车到达该处时，那名警察将左脚伸到车轮前，阻止车子移动。”

他回忆说，随后他向那些“大道”人员提出抗议。就在他这样做的时候，两名警察用手中的步枪威胁他。

妻子遭掌掴

与此同时，他的妻子被另一名警察拦住。少校回忆说，她也提出了抗议，用中文说了几句话，但他不懂中文，所以不明白意思。

据她后来透露，在她的抗议未被理睬时，一名警察询问彭尼斯顿夫人的国籍。“如果你是日本人，走吧，没关系，”据说那名警官是这样说的。

彭尼斯顿少校称，当她未回答这一询问时，那名警察狠狠地扇了她一记耳光，并未意识到她是一名日本女性。

为了保护妻子免受进一步的粗暴对待，彭尼斯顿少校冲上前去援助，并再次向警察强烈抗议。然而，他的抗议换来的是一记枪托击打，导致他的左前臂淤青。当时，其他警察也冲向他的妻子，朝她的肩膀猛击数下，撕裂了她的皮草大衣。

伪警介入

就在此时，一名“大道”警察试图制止争端。少校称，趁此机会，他协助妻子、孩子和阿妈继续前行，彭尼斯顿夫人仍在抗议。

显然被彭尼斯顿夫人在继续前往公园途中所说的中文激怒，此前负责扇她耳光的两名警官再次气势汹汹地向她冲来。据信，一名身份无法查明的便衣中国人的及时介入，防止了对这对夫妇的其他袭击发生。

事发后，彭尼斯顿少校向静安寺捕房报案。他说他将于今日向美国领事当局报告此事。

这位少校曾在《字林西报》任职。

6 4/12

Man Left Dying Under

Removal from Pavement
To Hospital Thwarted

A dying Chinese lay on the foot-path outside 11 Brenan Road, near Jessfield Road, for a matter of three hours on Friday night, guarded by a policeman of the Shanghai “Special Municipality,” it was revealed yesterday. He was finally abandoned towards midnight, when he was found to be dead.

The case came to the attention of the Settlement Police shortly after 8.30 o’clock, at which time a foreign sergeant on patrol spotted the prone figure on the pavement, with a Chinese Municipality constable standing guard. The foreigner could see that the man in the road, was in extremis.

The sergeant having reported his discovery, efforts were made by the Settlement Police to have the suffering Chinese removed to hospital. It is stated, however, that the Special Municipality constable refused to let anyone touch the man until he had received instructions from the headquarters of the Special Municipality Police at 92 Jessfield Road.

Finally, at 11.30 p.m., the constable abandoned the figure on the pavement. When the Settlement Police picked him up, the man was dead and he was so certified a few minutes later at St. Luke’s Hospital. The body was taken to the public mortuary. Death had apparently been due to illness.

Britons Held by
Chinese Police

Detained for Four Hours
After Trivial Accident on
Road Outside Perimeter

Detailed reports were made yesterday to the British Consular authorities regarding the detention of Mr. C. N. Abbott, British, of the Imperial Chemical Industries staff, and Mrs. Abbott by "Special Municipality" police on Wednesday. Mr. Abbott was held for 3 hours and 45 minutes, while his wife was detained for a shorter period.

Mr. and Mrs. Abbott were riding in Great Western Road, near the intersection of Warren Road, when Mr. Abbott's pony shied away from a motor car and backed into a Chinese on a bicycle. The cyclist was injured slightly, the fingers of one hand being bruised.

A policeman of the "Special Municipality" appeared on the scene and later was joined by two more constables. None of them could speak English, and Mr. and Mrs. Abbott could not explain in Chinese what had occurred. Mr. Abbott tried to inform them that he wanted to go back to the Great Western Road barrier for an interpreter. Mr. and Mrs. Abbott and the constables finally went together.

At the perimeter a British sentry realized the plight of the two foreigners and informed a foreign sergeant of the Shanghai Municipal Police. A report was made to the Bubbling Well Station, and the British Military Headquarters were also notified.

Mrs. Abbott Seized by Arm

Meanwhile several more "Special Municipality" policemen had joined the group, including an officer of this body. Mrs. Abbott wanted to cross the barrier into the British sector but was not allowed to do so by the "Special Municipality" police inspector, who is alleged to have seized her by the arm. It was not until a civilian foreigner had intervened in her behalf that she was allowed to go. With her pony she crossed the perimeter to the British side.

Mr. Abbott was finally taken to the "Special Municipality" Police Station in Great Western Road for questioning. He was held there until 2.45 p.m., when he was allowed to go home. The negotiations in the case were carried on by the Chinese, Japanese, Settlement Police and British Military. The officers who took part as representatives of the British Military Headquarters included Maj.-Gen. F. K. Simmons, commander of British Forces in the Shanghai area, and Major S. R. Hunt, liaison officer with the Japanese Forces.

在界外道路发生轻微事故后

昨日已向英国领事当局提交了关于周三帝国化学工业公司（Imperial Chemical Industries）职员、英国人 C. N. Abbott 先生及其夫人被“特别市”警察拘留的详细报告。Abbott 先生被扣留了3小时45分钟，而其夫人被扣留的时间较短。

Abbott 夫妇当时正乘车行驶在大西路（Great Western Road）靠近华伦路（Warren Road）交汇处，Abbott 先生的小马因受惊避开一辆汽车，向后撞上了一名骑自行车的中国人。骑车人受了轻伤，一只手的手指挫伤。

一名“特别市”警察出现在现场，随后又有两名巡警加入。他们都不会说英语，而 Abbott 夫妇也无法用中文解释发生的情况。Abbott 先生试图告知他们，他想回到大西路关卡去找一名翻译。最后，Abbott 夫妇与几名巡警一同前往。

在关卡处，一名英国哨兵意识到这两名外国人的困境，并通知了上海公共租界工部局警务处的一名外国巡佐。此事已报告给静安寺捕房，同时也通知了英军司令部。

Abbott 夫人手臂被抓住

与此同时，又有几名“特别市”警察加入了这群人，其中包括该机构的一名警官。Abbott 夫人想穿过关卡进入英方区域，但“特别市”警察督察不允许她这样做，据称该督察抓住了她的手臂。直到一名外籍平民介入为她求情，她才被允许离开。她带着小马穿过界线到了英方一侧。

Abbott 先生最终被带到大西路的“特别市”警察局接受讯问。他被扣留在那里直到下午2点45分，随后被允许回家。此案的交涉由中国方面、日本方面、租界警方和英军共同进行。作为英军司令部代表参与此事的军官包括上海地区英军司令 F. K. Simmons 少将，以及驻日军联络官 S. R. Hunt 少校。

(批：礼 10/20)

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
OCT 16 1939
Council Asking Consuls
To Act Against Ta Tao
'Outside Road' Invasion
CITY GOVERNMENT ACTION
TO POLICE STREETS, GET
TAXES REPORTED TO BODY
Consuls-General Meeting Expected
With Ta Tao policemen continuing to duplicate Shanghai
Municipal Police traffic posts and still manning sandbag barri-
cades on municipal pavements, as part of their attempts to
seize the rich revenue of the outside roads area, appeal had
been made by the SMC to the Consular Body over the affair.
Consuls-General of the foreign Powers are considering the
matter at present, and it is be-
lieved that they will hold a con-
ference on the matter in the near
future.
Economic Affair
Although on the face of it a
political affair, efforts by the Ta
Tao authority to take the area
from the SMC has great economic
significance. In the first half of
this year rates and taxes collected
by the SMC totalled $528,642, while
the budget for the year estimated
total collection at $932,000, al-
though it is quite possible that it
may hit the million.
Invasion by the Japanese spon-
sored regime is considered to be
aimed more at the cash than at
the political angle, as the Ta Tao
subsidy from Nanking was recent-
ly halted.
SMC Attitude
Attitude of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council towards the outside
roads is that they were built by
the SMC on land purchased by the
SMC under rights conferred by
existing regulations, and that
dwellers alongside the road have
to pay rates and taxes.
Moreover, dwellers in lanes off
the road who have access to muni-
cipal drainage systems, or to light
and water facilities made possible
by the SMC must pay the same
rates. Recent attempts have been
made by Ta Tao authorities also
to collect rates in the area, al-
though with what degree of suc-
cess has not been announced.
Municipal Services
The SMC looks after the roads
in the area, provides fire depart-
ment service, and even is taking
health and cleansing measures
well of the roads itself, so control

ture of a considerable sum of
money.
Up to the present Ta Tao inter-
ference has taken the form of at-
tempting to usurp police functions
from the SMP, despite promises

function off the roads. Recent
developments have included the
attempt to take over control of
two traffic lights, at Edinburgh
intersections with Great Western
and Yu Yuen Roads, and an ulti-
matum to the Police that these
lights should not function as from
today, which was ignored. This
is in addition to sending bills for
Ta Tao rates and taxes.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》。
1939年10月16日
公董局请求领事团
对大道“越界筑路”入侵采取行动
市政府行动
整治街道、征收税款之事已报告给该机构
预计将与领事团举行会议

鉴于大道（Ta Tao）警察继续 duplicating（原文如此，意为重复设置/仿设）上海公共租界工部局警务处的交通岗亭，并在租界人行道上驻守沙袋路障，作为其企图攫取越界筑路区域丰厚收入的一部分，工部局已就此事件向领事团提出呼吁。
各外国列强的总领事目前正在审议此事，相信他们将在近期就此召开一次会议。

经济事务
虽然表面上看这是一起政治事件，但大道当局试图从工部局手中夺取该区域具有重大的经济意义。今年上半年，工部局征收的捐税总额为528,642美元，而本年度预算估计征收总额为932,000美元，尽管完全有可能达到一百万美元。
由日本支持的政权进行的入侵被认为更多是针对现金而非政治角度，因为南京方面最近停止了对大道的补贴。

工部局的态度
上海公共租界工部局对越界筑路区域的态度是，这些道路是工部局根据现行法规赋予的权利购买土地后修建的，因此沿路居民必须缴纳捐税。
此外，通过弄堂接入工部局排水系统，或使用由工部局提供的照明和供水设施的沿街弄堂居民，也必须缴纳相同的捐税。大道当局最近也试图在该区域征收捐税，但其成功程度尚未公布。

市政服务
工部局负责该区域的道路维护，提供消防部门服务，甚至在该区域本身采取卫生和清洁措施，因此控制这些区域不仅意味着收取收入，还意味着支出相当可观的资金。
迄今为止，大道的干涉形式一直是试图篡夺工部局警务处的警察职能，尽管此前曾承诺大道人员只会在越界筑路区域以外活动。最近的事态发展包括试图接管爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）与大西路及愚园路交汇处的两个交通信号灯的控制权，并向警方发出最后通牒，要求这些信号灯从今天起停止运作，但该通牒被无视。此外，他们还寄来了大道捐税的账单。

CHINA PRESS
OCT 7 1939

Paging Washington And London

THE Shanghai Municipal Council needs the support of the foreign powers interested in the International Settlement in settling the outside road impasse. Unless this support is given promptly and in an unmistakable fashion, an extremely undesirable precedent, detrimental to the status of all the foreign controlled areas in China, is likely to be established.

This newspaper does not intend at this moment to delve into complicated legal and diplomatic phases of the outside road problem. It is sufficient to point out that when all the facts are boiled down to their bare essentials, the “Ta Tao” policemen have no right to be on the extra-Settlement roads.

The “Ta Tao” regime or the so-called “Special Municipality of Greater Shanghai” is not an organization representing the legally recognized government of China. Its policemen are able to take up their posts on extra-Settlement roads merely because they happen to have guns, and because the Shanghai Municipal Council is not disposed or in a position to use similarly forcible measures in dislodging them.

* * *

IF we are inclined to use high-flown terms, we may correctly and with justification use the word “invasion” in describing the action of the “Ta Tao” policemen. That indeed is what the action of the “Ta Tao” policemen really amounts to, and there is no reason why the foreign powers interested in the Settlement should continue to refrain from recognizing and calling a spade a spade.

Having sent its armed men to patrol and occupy the roads, the “Ta Tao” regime is now starting negotiations with the Shanghai Municipal Council with the hope that their “invasion” and the de facto status of the outside road will be consecrated by a formal agreement and officially recognized.

The Shanghai Municipal Council, which derives its authority and support from the various powers, is in a pathetic quandary. Unable to take a firm stand because of the lack of support, the Council has been compelled to make one concession after another. This series of retreats has already enabled the “Ta Tao” agents to have the run of the field in the outside road area. Unless some support is given immediately, the Council will ultimately find it necessary to bow to force and to recognize the “right” of the “Ta Tao” regime in the western outside road districts.

* * *

THE status of the extra-Settlement road affects today not only the status of the International Settlement and the French Concession but also the fate of all foreign controlled areas in China. This is true because the outside road impasse involves the question of the legality of the puppet regimes.

If the “Ta Tao” policemen are allowed to continue their occupation and if an agreement is finally reached which concedes to the “Ta Tao” regime the right to collect taxes in the outside road area, this would mean in effect that the Shanghai Municipal Council and the foreign powers interested in the Settlement have bestowed their official recognition on the puppet “government.”

It would also mean—if concession is made to the “Ta Tao” regime—that the powers have formally recognized the fact that the puppet governments have a legitimate claim on the foreign-controlled areas.

* * *

FROM such a de facto or de jure recognition it will be easy to lead to the next step. As soon as a formal agreement is reached, the “Ta Tao” regime in Shanghai and their counterparts in other cities of China will immediately start agitating for the immediate return of all the foreign settlements and concessions. If events in the future should take such a turn, the foreign powers would indeed have no one but themselves to blame because it was the concession in the outside road areas which led to such a development.

On the outside road question, the Shanghai Municipal Council must not be left in the lurch by the foreign powers. It must be given prompt and full support by the powers because unless such support is forthcoming, the Council will be compelled to capitulate and be forced to take part in establishing a dangerous precedent which in future will form the basis for further encroachment upon foreign rights and interests in China.

《字林西报》（China Press）
1939年10月7日

呼吁华盛顿与伦敦介入

上海公共租界工部局需要那些对国际租界有利害关系的列强提供支持，以解决越界筑路地区的僵局。除非迅速且明确地给予这种支持，否则极有可能树立一个极不受欢迎的先例，从而损害中国所有外国控制区域的地位。

本报此刻无意深入探讨越界筑路问题中复杂的法律和外交层面。只需指出，当将所有事实提炼为最核心的要素时，“大道”警察无权出现在租界以外的道路上。

“大道”政权或所谓的“上海特别市”并非代表中国合法公认政府的组织。其警察之所以能够占据越界道路上的岗位，仅仅是因为他们持有枪支，且上海公共租界工部局既无意愿也无能力采取类似的强力措施将其驱逐。

* * *

如果我们倾向于使用宏大的辞藻，我们可以正确且有理由地使用“入侵”一词来描述“大道”警察的行动。这确实就是“大道”警察行动的真实实质，那些对租界有利害关系的列强没有理由继续回避正视这一事实并直言不讳。

在派遣武装人员巡逻并占领道路后，“大道”政权现在开始与上海公共租界工部局进行谈判，希望其“入侵”行为及越界道路的既成事实能通过正式协议得到确认并获得官方承认。

上海公共租界工部局的权力和支持来源于各列强，目前正处于一种可怜的困境之中。由于缺乏支持而无法采取坚定立场，工部局被迫做出一次又一次的让步。这一系列退让已经使“大道”代理人得以在越界道路区域肆意妄为。除非立即获得某些支持，否则工部局最终将不得不向武力低头，并承认“大道”政权在西部越界道路区域的“权利”。

* * *

越界道路的地位今天不仅影响国际租界和法租界的地位，也影响中国所有外国控制区域的命运。这是因为越界道路僵局涉及伪政权的合法性问题。

如果允许“大道”警察继续其占领行为，并且最终达成一项协议， conceding（让步/承认）“大道”政权在越界道路区域征税的权利，这实际上意味着上海公共租界工部局和对租界有利害关系的列强已给予该傀儡“政府”官方承认。

这也意味着——如果对“大道”政权做出让步——列强已正式承认伪政府对外国控制区域拥有合法主张的事实。

* * *

从这种事实上的或法律上的承认出发，很容易走向下一步。一旦达成正式协议，上海的“大道”政权及其在中国其他城市的对应机构将立即开始鼓动立即收回所有外国租界和租借地。如果未来事态如此发展，列强确实只能怪罪自己，因为正是越界道路区域的让步导致了这样的事态发展。

在越界道路问题上，上海公共租界工部局绝不能被列强抛弃不管。它必须得到列强迅速而充分的支持，因为除非提供此类支持，否则工部局将被迫投降，并被迫参与建立一个危险的先例，这将在未来成为进一步侵蚀外国在华权益的基础。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.
OCT 1 4 1939

Mayor Fu's Police
Interfere in West

"Special Municipality"
Men Order Traffic Lights
Out in Edinburgh Road

Members of the "Special Municipality Police" under Mr. Fu Siao-en, ordered British Indian constables of the Settlement Police to switch off the S.M.P. traffic lights at two important crossings in Edinburgh Road at 10:40 o'clock yesterday morning, thus causing temporary confusion at these intersections and a quasi-incident which was settled when police reinforcements were rushed to the two places from Bubbling Well Station, and the "Special Municipality Police" finally withdrew their augmented force.

The attempt on the part of the Kiangwan authorities to seize full control of the traffic situation along Edinburgh Road, in the British Military Defence Sector, was made without warning when squads of their "police" equipped with rifles marched up to the Sikh constables on duty and ordered them to turn off the regular traffic lights at the two intersections. The Indians were forced to comply with the demand and, as soon as they were able to leave their posts, communicated by the S.M.P. street telephone with Bubbling Well Station, whence squads of foreigners and Chinese were immediately sent to the scene.

Light Signals Resumed

It was estimated that the control light at Yu Yuen and Edinburgh Roads was off for about three minutes while the one at Great Western and Edinburgh Roads was out of operation for about ten. At any rate, with the appearance of about twenty extra S.M.P. men at each crossing the "Special Municipality" constables promptly made way for the Settlement Police to resume their guidance of the red-and-green semaphores. After about an hour all the additional Kiangwan constables were withdrawn from both intersections (including one man carrying a species of sub-machine gun, at Yu Yuen and Edinburgh Roads), and a short time later the S.M.P. recalled their reinforcements.

Meanwhile, senior police officers had arrived and inspected the two crossings as well as the intersection of Edinburgh and Tunsin Roads, where the "Special Municipality" had increased their squad of men. Mr. R. W. Yorke and Mr. A. H. Samson, Assistant Commissioners, were on the scene with other high officials of the S.M.P.

A personal inspection of the localities involved was made also by Major-General F. Keith-Simmons, Commander of British Forces in the Shanghai Area, and Major B. H. Ashmore, Brigade Major.

Shortly after the incident, truckloads of "Special Municipality" uniformed men, equipped with rifles, toured the district, pausing at the important crossings. These men did not alight from their lorries, however, at the Edinburgh Road intersections.

《字林西报》（North China Daily News）
1939年10月14日

傅市长之警察
干涉西区

“特别市”人员
命令爱丁堡路
交通信号灯熄灭

昨日上午10时40分，傅筱庵先生麾下的“特别市警察”成员命令租界巡捕房的英籍印度巡捕关闭爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）两个重要交叉口的工部局警务处（S.M.P.）交通信号灯，导致这些路口暂时混乱，并引发了一起 quasi-incident（准事件/类冲突事件）。当静安寺分局（Bubbling Well Station）迅速向两地增派警力后，该事件得以解决，“特别市警察”最终撤回了其增援部队。

江湾当局企图全面控制爱丁堡路（位于英军防御区内）交通状况的尝试是在毫无预警的情况下进行的，当时他们配备步枪的“警察”小队走向正在执勤的锡克教巡捕，命令他们关闭两个交叉口的常规交通信号灯。印度巡捕被迫服从要求，一旦能够离开岗位，便通过工部局警务处的街道电话与静安寺分局联系，分局随即派遣外籍和华人小队立即赶赴现场。

恢复信号灯光

据估计，愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）与爱丁堡路交叉口的控制灯熄灭了约三分钟，而大西路（Great Western Road）与爱丁堡路交叉口的灯则停止运作了约十分钟。无论如何，随着每个路口出现约二十名额外的工部局警务处人员，“特别市”巡捕迅速为租界巡捕让路，使其恢复对红绿臂板信号机的指挥。约一小时后，所有增援的江湾巡捕均从两个交叉口撤离（其中包括一名在愚园路与爱丁堡路路口携带某种冲锋枪的人员），不久之后，工部局警务处也召回了其增援部队。

与此同时，高级警务官员已抵达现场，视察了这两个交叉口以及爱丁堡路与同信路（Tunsin Road，音译）的交叉口，后者也是“特别市”增加人手的地方。助理总监 R. W. Yorke 先生和 A. H. Samson 先生与其他工部局警务处高官一同在现场。

上海地区英军司令 F. Keith-Simmons 少将和旅参谋长 B. H. Ashmore 少校也对涉事地点进行了亲自视察。

事件发生后不久，满载身着制服、配备步枪的“特别市”人员的卡车在该地区巡回，并在重要交叉口停留。然而，这些人并未在爱丁堡路的交叉口下车。

（批注：Like ( 14/10 ）

CHINA PRESS.

OCT 8 1939

Bus Searching
Is Started By
Local Puppets

Omnibus Boarded Near
Hollywood By Six
“Ta Tao” Men

“Ta Tao” police in plainclothes yesterday started searching buses of the China General Omnibus Company on extra-Settlement roads. This is according to information obtained by THE CHINA PRESS from reliable sources last night.

The first case of its kind occurred on Yu Yuen Road directly in front of the Hollywood Gardens. The time was about 4.15 p.m. and the number of the bus board was 15149.

15-Minute Search

Eye-witnesses and passengers of the bus afterwards stated that six men in plainclothes, some of whom were armed, entered the bus as it stopped near the Hollywood Gardens and started to search everybody on board.

The search lasted about 15 minutes after which the intruders left the vehicle and permitted it to proceed. The Shanghai Municipal Police were subsequently notified and an investigation was launched.

Members of the search party are stated to have informed some of the passengers that they were “Ta Tao” policemen and were looking for guns. They found none.

Throwing a large section of the western district into a panic, “Ta Tao” policemen, led by Japanese gendarmes, staged “war games” on the stretch of land between Columbia Circle and Amherst Avenue yesterday afternoon.

Gardens Trampled

The “war games” got under way at approximately 2.30 p.m., when more than 50 “Ta Tao” gendarmes, armed with rifles and machine-guns, fired blank cartridges, trampled gardens and vegetable fields under foot, and halted all traffic in this area for more than 30 minutes.

The “Ta Tao” policemen were still there after 3 p.m., but the maneuvers had finished by that time.

The “war games” were staged well within “Ta Tao” territory, it was reported to THE CHINA PRESS by a foreign eye-witness, who stated that in his opinion several hundred rounds of blank shots were fired.

Well-informed circles commenting on the “war maneuvers” yesterday held the view that the operation was a demonstration to impress badlands gangsters.

（批：Liu 6/10）

1939年10月8日

本地傀儡开始
搜查公交车

六名“大道”人员
在好莱坞附近
登上公交车

据《字林西报》昨晚从可靠消息来源获悉，“大道”警察昨日开始便衣搜查越界道路上的中国通用汽车公司（China General Omnibus Company）的公交车。

首例此类事件发生在好莱坞花园（Hollywood Gardens）正对面的愚园路。时间约为下午4点15分，被搜查的公交车车牌号为15149。

搜查持续15分钟

目击者和该车乘客事后陈述，六名便衣男子（其中一些人携带武器）在公交车停靠在好莱坞花园附近时上车，并开始搜查车上所有人。

搜查持续了约15分钟，随后闯入者离开车辆并允许其继续行驶。随后通知了上海公共租界工部局警务处，并展开了调查。

据称，搜查组成员告知部分乘客，他们是“大道”警察，正在搜寻枪支。结果一无所获。

昨日午后，由日本宪兵带领的“大道”警察在哥伦比亚圈（Columbia Circle）与安赫斯特大道（Amherst Avenue）之间的一片土地上上演“战争游戏”，令西区大片区域陷入恐慌。

花园遭践踏

“战争游戏”大约在下午2点30分开始，当时50多名配备步枪和机枪的“大道”宪兵发射空包弹，践踏花园和蔬菜田，并导致该地区的交通中断超过30分钟。

下午3点后，“大道”警察仍在那里，但演习届时已结束。

一位外国目击者向《字林西报》报告称，“战争游戏”是在“大道”领土范围内上演的，他认为发射了数百发空包弹。

昨日评论此次“军事演习”的消息灵通人士认为，此次行动是一次旨在震慑不良地带帮派分子的示威。

（批注：Liu 6/10）

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS
OCT 7 193

Apology to H.M. Consulate
For Mr. Ward's Arrest

Japanese Evince Further Interest Yesterday in
His House ; Detailed Account of Proceedings

IN connection with the arrest and detention of Mr. James Ward,
employee of Reuters, Ltd., by the "Special Municipality" police
at his home at House 23, Lane 1984, Bubbling Well Road, on
Thursday night, a full apology was tendered to H.M. Consul-
General, Sir Herbert Phillips, by two officials of the Shanghai
"Special Municipality" who called on him yesterday afternoon.
The two officials were Mr. Lu Ying, Chief of Police of the
Shanghai Special Municipality, and Col. E. Igarashi, Chief Adviser
to the Shanghai "Special Municipality" Police Bureau. They were
received on behalf of the Consul-General by the Superintending
Consul, Mr. C. V. Kitson.
Mr. Lu Ying, speaking for the
Shanghai Special Municipality, apolo-
gized for the arrest and detention of
Mr. Ward. He informed the Superin-
tending Consul that the "Special
municipality" Police had entered Mr.
Ward's house not knowing it was the
property of a Third Power national
and had arrested him in ignorance
of the fact that he was a Briton.
The police official responsible for the
affair, he said, had been punished.
He assured the Superintending Con-
sul that there would be no recurrence
of such incidents and that there
would be no interference with British
nationals in the future. Mr. Lu Ying
guaranteed, on behalf of the Shang-
hai "Special Municipality," full pro-
tection for British residents in the
area under its jurisdiction.

Entry Forced

Meanwhile, the "North-China Daily
News" learned yesterday that a party
consisting of approximately ten men,
including two uniformed members of
the "Special Municipality" police rang
the bell of Mr. Ward's residence at
about 8 p.m., pushing their way into
the hall as soon as the door
had been opened. They demanded to
inspect the premises, whereupon Mr.
Ward asked for a warrant to be pro-
duced. While a few members of the
group left the building, presumably
to obtain the warrant, the remainder
commenced a search subsequently
discovering a small room containing
a wireless transmitter which was
quickly dismantled and seized.
This room, it was learned, had been
rented to a certain Mr. Wang whose
activities were unknown to Mr. Ward
as the only contact which he had
with his tenant, was that of collecting
the rental at the end of each month.
The discovery of the transmitter,
however, resulted in Mr. Ward's ar-
rest. He was taken to the "Special
Municipality" police station, Jessfield
Road, and was interrogated. He was
even asked to divulge the salary
which he was being paid by Messrs.
Reuters, Ltd.'
During the period of his detention,
Mr. Ward was moved to various
houses in the vicinity on two occa-
sions, being finally led to a room
where he was being watched by an
armed policeman.

（批：File C 7/10）

1939年10月7日

就沃德先生被捕向英领馆致歉

日本人昨日对其住宅表现出进一步兴趣；事件详细经过

关于路透社有限公司雇员詹姆斯·沃德先生于周四晚在其位于静安寺路1984弄23号的家中被“特别市”警察逮捕和拘留一事，上海“特别市”的两名官员昨日下午拜访了英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士，并向其致以全面道歉。
这两名官员是上海特别市警察局局长卢英和上海“特别市”警察局首席顾问五十岚大佐。他们由监理领事C. V. 基特森先生代表总领事接待。
卢英先生代表上海特别市发言，为逮捕和拘留沃德先生表示歉意。他告知监理领事，“特别市”警察进入沃德先生住宅时，并不知道这是第三国国民的财产，并在不知其为英国人的情况下将其逮捕。他说，负责此事的警官已受到惩处。他向监理领事保证，此类事件不会再次发生，未来也不会干扰英国国民。卢英先生代表上海“特别市”保证，对其管辖区域内的英国居民提供充分保护。

强行进入

与此同时，《字林西报》昨日获悉，一支由大约十人组成的队伍，其中包括两名身穿制服的“特别市”警察，于晚上8点左右按响了沃德先生住所的门铃，门一打开就挤进大厅。他们要求检查该处，于是沃德先生要求出示搜查令。当该团伙中的几名成员离开大楼（据推测是去获取搜查令）时，其余人员开始搜查，随后发现一个小房间，里面有一台无线发射机，该发射机迅速被拆卸并扣押。
据了解，这个房间租给了一个姓王的先生，沃德先生对其活动一无所知，因为他与租客的唯一联系就是每月底收取租金。
然而，发现发射机导致沃德先生被捕。他被带到极司菲尔路的“特别市”警察局并接受讯问。他甚至被要求透露路透社有限公司支付给他的薪水数额。
在被拘留期间，沃德先生两次被转移到附近的各处房屋，最后被带到一个房间，由一名武装警察看守。

（批注：档案 C 7/10）

S.M.P. Intervene

High Settlement Police officials informed the British Consul-General of the affair and Mr. Ward was released shortly after midnight.

Despite yesterday's apology, however, the authorities in control of the "outside roads" districts evinced considerable interest for Mr. Ward's home yesterday. The building was photographed from outside and from within and two or three persons, believed to have been Japanese, called at the house on a number of occasions yesterday and asked the servants when they expected Mr. Ward to return.

Shortly after noon yesterday, two cars filled with Japanese or Chinese arrived at the house and made similar enquiries whereupon they departed.

Meanwhile, Mr. Ward did not return to his home yesterday and asked his servants to bring his belongings to an address in the Central District, where he is temporarily staying pending the settlement of the affair through official channels.

Questioned regarding the incident, a spokesman at yesterday's press conference stated that the "Special Municipality" police had heard that a Chinese, believed to be a Mr. Wang, was engaged in illegal radio communications with Chungking. In view of this report, the spokesman continued, a raid on the building in question was carried out.

As Mr. Ward was an athlete and sun-tanned, the spokesman added, and as he did not look like a foreigner, the detectives mistook him for Wang.

Moreover, the spokesman added, Mr. Ward's name, translated into Chinese means "flower" and "virtue" and is pronounced "Wah Te" which led to his being mistaken for the wanted man.

When his true identity was established, the spokesman concluded, the Special Municipality "took measures for his relief and an apology was made while disciplinary action was taken against those who took part in the raid.

工部局警务处介入

公共租界高级警务官员将此事通报英国总领事，沃德先生在午夜过后不久获释。

然而，尽管昨日已道歉，控制“越界筑路”地区的当局昨日对沃德先生的住宅表现出极大兴趣。有人从外部和内部对该建筑进行了拍照，昨天有数人（据信是日本人）多次到访该住宅，询问仆人预计沃德先生何时回来。

昨天中午刚过，两辆载满日本人或中国人的汽车到达该住宅，进行了类似的询问后离去。

与此同时，沃德先生昨天没有回家，而是让仆人将他的物品送到中央区的一个地址，他暂时住在那里，等待通过官方渠道解决此事。

在昨天的新闻发布会上，一位发言人在被问及此事时表示，“特别市”警察听说一名据信姓王的中国人正在与重庆进行非法无线电通讯。发言人继续说，鉴于这一报告，警方对涉案建筑进行了突击搜查。
发言人补充说，由于沃德先生是一名运动员且皮肤晒黑，看起来不像外国人，侦探们误以为他是王。
此外，发言人补充说，沃德先生的名字翻译成中文意为“花”和“德”，发音为“华德”（Wah Te），这导致他被误认为是通缉犯。
发言人最后总结道，当他的真实身份被确认后，特别市“采取了措施予以释放并道歉，同时对参与突袭的人员采取了纪律行动。”

1939

Apology Is Offered To
British Consulate For
Arrest Of Mr. J. Ward

Chief Of City Government Police Calls To See
Consul-General Yesterday Afternoon; Case
Of Mistaken Identity Is Revealed

BRITON MISTAKEN FOR MAN WHO HAD
SENT MESSAGES TO CHUNGKING

In connection with the arrest and detention of Mr James
Ward, employee of Reuters, Ltd., by the City Government Police
at his home at House 23, Lane 1984, Bubbling Well Road, on
Thursday night, a full apology was tendered to the British
Consul-General, Sir Herbert Phillips, by two officials of the
Shanghai Special Municipality who called at the British
Consulate-General yesterday afternoon.

The two officials were Mr. Lu Ying, Chief of Police of the
Shanghai Special Municipality, and Colonel E. Igarashi, Chief
Adviser of the Shanghai Special Municipality Police Bureau.
They were received on behalf of the Consul-General by the
Superintending Consul, Mr. G. V. Kitson.

Mr. Lu Ying, speaking for the
Shanghai Special Municipality,
apologized for the arrest and de-
tention of Mr. Ward.
He informed the Superintending
Consul that the City Police had
entered Mr. Ward's house not
knowing it was the property of a
Third-Power national and had
arrested him in ignorance of the
fact that he was a Briton. The
police official responsible for the
affair, he said, had been punished.
He assured the Superintending
Consul that there would be no
recurrence of such incidents and
that there would be no interference
with British nationals in the future.
Mr. Lu Ying guaranteed, on
behalf of the Shanghai Special
Municipality, full protection for
British residents in the area under
the jurisdiction of the Special
Municipality.

Forcibly Removed
Mr. Ward was allegedly forcibly
removed from his residence at
about 8.10 p.m. on Thursday and
not released until shortly after
midnight and then only after nego-
tiations had been conducted by
high ranking officers of the S.M.P.,
the British military and the British
Consulate.
At the time that Mr. Ward was
forcibly removed from his house
by officers of the City Government
Police, they also removed a wire-
less transmitting set he had in his
house as well as a typewriter and
took them together with him to their
headquarters at Nanking Road.

It was only after lengthy nego-
tiations that Mr. Ward was released
and the wireless set turned over to
the S.M.P. British authorities are
now conducting a full investigation
into the affair.

Mistaken Identity
"The arrest of Mr. James Ward
by the Special Municipality was
due to mistaken identity," the
Japanese Army spokesmen said at
the press conference last evening.
"The Special Municipality police
had heard that a man named Wang
had been engaged in illegal radio
communication with Chungking,'
said the spokesman. "In view of
the report, detectives staged a raid
on the premises in which the
alleged sending of communications
was taking place.
"On entering the premises the
detectives found an elaborate radio
sending and receiving apparatus.
They assumed Mr. Ward to be Mr.
Wang, the man they were looking
for, and took him to headquarters
for questioning.
"As stated in the newspapers, Mr.
Ward was an athlete and sun-
tanned. As he was of mixed par-
entage and did not look like a
foreigner, they mistook him for

《上海泰晤士报》

就J.沃德先生被捕向英国领事馆致歉

市政府警察局长昨日下午拜访总领事；揭露系认错人案件

英国人被误认为向重庆发送消息的人

关于路透社有限公司雇员詹姆斯·沃德先生于周四晚在其位于静安寺路1984弄23号的家中被市政府警察逮捕和拘留一事，上海特别市的两名官员昨日下午拜访英国总领事馆，向英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士致以全面道歉。
这两名官员是上海特别市警察局局长卢英和上海特别市警察局首席顾问五十岚大佐。他们由监理领事G. V. 基特森先生代表总领事接待。
卢英先生代表上海特别市发言，为逮捕和拘留沃德先生表示歉意。
他告知监理领事，市警察进入沃德先生住宅时，并不知道这是第三国国民的财产，并在不知其为英国人的情况下将其逮捕。他说，负责此事的警官已受到惩处。他向监理领事保证，此类事件不会再次发生，未来也不会干扰英国国民。卢英先生代表上海特别市保证，对特别市管辖区域内的英国居民提供充分保护。

被强行带走
据称，沃德先生于周四晚上8点10分左右被强行从其住所带走，直到午夜过后才获释，而且是在工部局警务处、英国军方和英国领事馆的高级官员进行谈判之后。
当市政府警察官员强行将沃德先生从其家中带走时，他们还拿走了他家中的一台无线发射装置以及一台打字机，并将它们连同他一起带到了南京路的总部。
经过长时间的谈判，沃德先生才获释，无线装置移交给工部局警务处。英国当局目前正在对此事进行全面调查。

认错人
“特别市逮捕詹姆斯·沃德先生是由于认错人，”日本陆军发言人在昨晚的新闻发布会上说。
发言人说：“特别市警察听说一个叫王的人一直在与重庆进行非法无线电通讯。鉴于这一报告，侦探们对据称发送通讯的场所进行了突袭。
“进入该场所后，侦探们发现了一套复杂的无线电收发设备。他们假定沃德先生就是他们正在寻找的王先生，并将他带到总部进行讯问。
“正如报纸所述，沃德先生是一名运动员且皮肤晒黑。由于他是混血儿，看起来不像外国人，他们误以为他是王。”
当确定沃德先生不是通缉犯时，特别市采取了释放他的措施并给予了道歉，同时对参与突袭的人员采取了纪律行动。

上海特别市两名官员昨日下午前往英国总领事馆，就周四晚间“大道”警察逮捕并拘留路透社有限公司雇员詹姆斯·沃德（James Ward）先生一事，向英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）致以充分歉意。

这两名官员分别是“大道”警察局局长陆英（Lu Ying，音译）先生，以及上海“特别市政府警察局”首席顾问五十岚大佐（Colonel E. Igarashi）。他们由英国总监事基特森先生（Mr. G. V. Kitson）代表赫伯特爵士予以接见。陆英代表其机构，为逮捕和拘留沃德先生一事表示道歉。

他告知基特森先生，“大道”警察进入沃德先生住宅时，并不知道该处房产属于第三国国民，且在不知其为英国人的情况下将其逮捕。他说，对此事负责的“大道”官员已受到惩处。

陆英向英国官员保证，此类事件不会重演，今后也不会干扰英国国民。陆英还代表上海“特别市政府”保证，对“特别市政府”管辖区域内的英国居民提供全面保护。

并非棒球明星

与此同时，昨日有人否认被“大道”警察拘留的沃德是当地著名的足球和棒球明星詹姆斯·沃德先生，《字林西报》昨日曾误报为此人。《字林西报》对此错误表示遗憾。

对沃德先生住宅的突袭是昨晚日本新闻发布会上的质询主题。日本军方发言人称，“大道”警察正在搜寻一名姓王的中国人，此人涉嫌与重庆保持非法无线电通讯。他们确实查获了一台无线电发报机，但已移交给英国当局。

CHINA PRESS.
OCT 5 1939
258.3

British Doctor Detained Two
Hours By ‘Ta Tao’ Policemen

To Dr. John Gray, British, 934 Bubbling Well Road, goes the distinction of being the first foreigner to become involved in a serious altercation with “Ta Tao” traffic police now usurping S.M.P. duties on extra-Settlement roads of the Western District.

Dr. Gray was stopped and detained by “Ta Tao” police near the corner of Tifeng and Bubbling Well Roads about 6 p.m. yesterday. He was released two hours later.

The doctor was driving his car along Bubbling Well Road when a “Ta Tao” traffic policeman standing at the intersection of that street and Tifeng Road suddenly ordered the machine to stop. The puppet policeman asked for the doctor’s driving license and the doctor refused to produce it.

“I obey only S.M.C. regulations on this street,” the doctor is credited with having told the “Ta Tao” policeman.

This reply seemed to infuriate the “Ta Tao” man who summoned help. Within a matter of seconds, some 40 “Ta Tao” policemen, most of them armed with rifles, surrounded Dr. Gray’s car. He was ordered to remain in the machine but two women were permitted to go.

The ensuing argument is reported to have been rather heated and resulted in the doctor’s being detained until about 8 p.m. Members of the Shanghai Municipal Police were responsible for terminating the dispute. They appeared on the scene just a few minutes after the argument started and after considerable discussion, were successful in obtaining “Ta Tao,” permission for the doctor to go home.

Lil

居住在静安寺路934号的英国人约翰·格雷博士（Dr. John Gray），成为第一位在西区越界筑路上与目前篡夺工部局警务职责的“大道”交通警察发生严重冲突的外国人。

当时，这位医生正驾车沿静安寺路行驶，一名站在该街与提丰路交叉口的“大道”交通警察突然命令车辆停下。这名伪警察要求查看医生的驾驶执照，医生拒绝出示。

据称，医生对“大道”警察说：“在这条街上，我只服从工部局的规定。”

这一回答似乎激怒了那名“大道”警察，他随即呼叫支援。几秒钟内，约40名“大道”警察，其中大多数持有步枪，包围了格雷博士的汽车。他被命令留在车内，但允许两名女性离开。

SHANGHAI TIMES
OCT 5 1939

City Police
Hold Briton
For 2 Hours

Mr. John Gray Involved
In Traffic Dispute
In West Area

Mr. John Gray, well-known local British consulting engineer and marine and cargo surveyor, was detained for nearly two hours by Shanghai City Government police yesterday evening on Bubbling Well Road, near the intersection of Tifeng Road, following an argument with a member of the City Government police over an alleged traffic infringement.

Mr. Gray was proceeding to his residence on Hungjao Road in his car at about 6.10 p.m. when he was halted by a City Government policeman on traffic duty at the corner of Bubbling Well and Tifeng Roads for allegedly disobeying a traffic signal. Mr. Gray's car, which was proceeding east to west along Bubbling Well Road, narrowly avoided colliding with a car traveling North to South across the intersection of Bubbling Well and Tifeng Roads, after which he was ordered to stop by the policemen.

Denies Guilt

Firmly denying that he was guilty of any traffic infringement Mr. Gray refused to accompany the constable to the City Government's new station on Jessfield Road, near Bubbling Well Road Police Station, whereupon the latter called for reinforcements.

Forty or 50 heavily armed City Government policemen quickly arrived on the scene, followed by members of Bubbling Well Station, under Inspector Dudley, officer in charge of the station, and negotiations were conducted on the spot as Mr. Gray still firmly refused to leave. There were three other persons in the car at the time of the incident, a Mr. MacDonald and two ladies, but while Mr. MacDonald remained with Mr. Gray throughout the entire proceedings, the ladies were permitted to leave almost immediately.

Finally, shortly before 8 p.m., Mr. Gray was permitted to continue his belated journey homewards. It is believed that a protest will be filed with the British Consular authorities over the affair.

市警察

约翰·格雷先生卷入

当地著名的英国咨询工程师及海事和货物检验师约翰·格雷先生，昨晚在静安寺路靠近提丰路路口处，因与一名市政府警察就涉嫌违反交通规则发生争执，被上海市政府警察拘留近两小时。

下午6点10分左右，格雷先生正驾车前往其虹桥路住所，在静安寺路与提丰路路口执勤的一名市政府警察以涉嫌不服从交通信号为由将其拦停。格雷先生的车沿静安寺路由东向西行驶，在穿过静安寺路与提丰路路口时，险些与一辆由北向南行驶的汽车相撞，随后警察命令其停车。

否认有罪

格雷先生坚决否认自己有任何违反交通规则的行为，并拒绝随警员前往位于静安寺路警察局附近的杰斯菲尔德路上的市政府新分局。于是该警员呼叫增援。

四五十名全副武装的市政府警察迅速赶到现场，随后静安寺路分局人员在分局主管达德利督察（Inspector Dudley）的带领下也到达现场。由于格雷先生仍坚决拒绝离开，现场进行了谈判。事发时车内还有另外三人，即麦克唐纳先生（Mr. MacDonald）和两位女士，但在整个过程中麦克唐纳先生一直陪伴格雷先生，而两位女士则被允许几乎立即离开。

最终，在晚上8点前不久，格雷先生获准继续其迟归的回家行程。据悉，将就此事向英国领事当局提出抗议。

伯顿副巡长（D.S.I. Burton）、永宗副巡长（D.S. Nagamune）和华人侦探22号（C.D.S. 22）在上述地址进行了查询。

西端花园65号由朱伯輝（Tsz Poh Wei）先生及其家人居住。他52岁，通州人，职业为棉花商人。该处所已缴纳工部局捐税。

据朱馬氏（Mrs. Tsz Mao Ss）称，1939年9月22日上午6点30分左右，两名特别市政府警察局官员和两名便衣男子通过敞开的前门进入屋内。其中一名穿制服者携带步枪，另一名穿着西式服装。这伙人询问是否有一名姓朱的男子住在这里，当得知确有此人后，他们上楼房间进行了粗略搜查。当被问及屋内是否有枪支时，得到的回答是没有。在一个房间里，他们发现朱伯輝先生躺在床上，并告诉他一名叫丁（Ting）的通州人已被捕，他（朱）必须陪同

23rd. September, 39.

1.

Re one male Chinese detained by the P.S.B. after being arrested in Case S. 3309 on Jessfield Road.

At 12noon 23/9/39, C.P.S. 3309 came to the Charge Room and reported that he had arrested one male Chinese on Jessfield Road near Connaught Road but later the arrested Chinese was taken to the P.S.B. sub-station on Singapore Road by 3 policemen attached to the P.S.B.

From enquiries made by C.D.S. 278 and the undersigned the following were ascertained:-

At about 9a.m. 23/9/39, one P. S.B. watchman named Chow Wah Yien (趙華也) employed for Sing Hang Li (新康里) off Jessfield Road witnessed in the alleyway one male Chinese named Lee Yung Shih (李永世), 16, Susih, stealing complainant of 3 pounds of waste thread value $50.00.

Complainant Kwong Hau Siew Mei (高小妹), of No. 86 Kung Kau Li (康高宅), off Connaught Road informed the watchman of this case, and upon being apprehended by the watchman, the suspect attempted to run away on to the Jessfield Road near Connaught Road where he was arrested by C.P.S. 3309, and taken thence to the P.S.B. sub-station on Singapore Road.

关于一名中国男子在杰斯菲尔德路（Jessfield Road）S. 3309 号案件中被捕后由警务处（P.S.B.）拘留一事。

1939年9月23日中午12时，巡捕房特别处警员第3309号（C.P.S. 3309）来到值班室报告称，他在杰斯菲尔德路靠近康纳路（Connaught Road）处逮捕了一名中国男子，但随后该被捕中国人被三名隶属于警务处（P.S.B.）的警察带往新加坡路（Singapore Road）的警务处分所。

经刑事侦缉处第278号（C.D.S. 278）及本报告人查询，查明情况如下：

1939年9月23日上午9时许，受雇于杰斯菲尔德路新康里（Sing Hang Li）的一名警务处（P.S.B.）更夫周华也（Chow Wah Yien，趙華也），在弄堂内目睹一名名叫李永世（Lee Yung Shih，李永世）、16岁、籍贯苏州的中国男子，正在盗窃报案人重达3磅、价值50.00美元的废线。

住在康纳路康高宅（Kung Kau Li）86号的报案人高小妹（Kwong Hau Siew Mei，高小妹）将此案告知更夫，嫌疑人在被更夫抓获时企图逃跑，逃至杰斯菲尔德路靠近康纳路处，被巡捕房特别处警员第3309号逮捕，随后被带往新加坡路的警务处分所。
